notes: Found SIMCom's official SIM7500_SIM7600 Series AT Command Manual (HTTP(S) AT Commands chapter) instead of continuing to reverse-engineer this from garbled transcripts. Confirms the chunked '+HTTPREAD: DATA,<n>' response format this code has been parsing was correct all along -- but also reveals every HTTP-related AT command's documented 'Maximum Response Time' is 120000ms (AT+HTTPINIT, AT+HTTPTERM, AT+HTTPACTION, AT+HTTPREAD), while this code was using guessed timeouts far shorter than that (3-5s for INIT/TERM, ~10-15s for a response this size for READ). Under real-world/slow network conditions, cutting a still-in-progress transfer off early looks identical to data corruption. Fixed: HTTP_CMD_TIMEOUT_MS = 120000 now used for AT+HTTPINIT/HTTPTERM/HTTPACTION and as the floor for AT+HTTPREAD's timeout (previously max(10000, length*4), now max(120000, length*4)); AT+HTTPPARA/HTTPSSL/HTTPDATA bumped from 3-5s to 15s. The rxbuf fix (0.6.3) and dedicated length-tracked reader (0.6.4) stay in place regardless -- this addresses a separate, real gap (timeouts too short vs the modem's own documented limits) rather than replacing them.
